quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It makes it hard to think clearly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or act foolishly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination and balance, and makes it hard to judge distances. This makes it difficult to react to what is happening around you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before you move.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or leaving a freeway. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers the rules they must follow. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower decision-making.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: Which action is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Leaving early to get to an appointment on time
Resting instead of driving when you are tired
Texting on your cell phone
Asking a passenger to control your GPS

questions.explanation: It is illegal to read or send text messages while driving because it takes your attention away from the road.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Drive around a lowered gate if no train is coming.
Stop at least 10 feet from the nearest rail.
Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing.
Always expect to see a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the rail when warning lights are flashing. Come to a complete stop if you see a train, hear its whistle, see a stop sign, or see lowered gates. Never drive through, around, or under a lowered gate.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not worry since all vehicles work the same way.
Hide that you do not know how to use it.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to operate it before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to operate it before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: When encountering an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them in return.
Show them you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Your vehicle must be inspected once a year:

options.text: Unless it is brand new.
To make sure it is safe to drive.
Only if it is older than five years.
Only if it is older than 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: To make sure it is safe to drive.
questions.explanation: All vehicles need an annual inspection to ensure they are working properly and are safe to drive.

questions.question: You miss your turn or exit on a freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: Which action is NOT safe when passing another vehicle?

options.text: Leaving less than four feet between your vehicle and the vehicle you are passing.
Giving a bicycle extra room when you pass it.
Using your turn signal before changing lanes to pass.
Checking your mirrors and looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaving less than four feet between your vehicle and the vehicle you are passing.
questions.explanation: You must leave at least four feet of space between your vehicle and the vehicle you are passing. Be extra careful when passing bicycles on the road.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions can greatly affect your driving ability. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can reduce your concentration on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to risk driving while emotionally upset.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You and another vehicle arrive at the same time. The other vehicle is to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until that vehicle has safely passed before you proceed.

questions.question: You see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. This protects them from injury.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means that you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. Your full attention is needed to drive safely. Any additional task can create a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and road markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective action you can take to reduce your risk of death or injury in a crash.
